name: EgoMimic
summary: EgoMimic collects egocentric human demonstrations with Aria glasses, normalizes them into the same observation and action representation the robot uses (3D hand pose standing in for end-effector pose, with the human arm visually masked out), and simply co-trains one policy over both streams. Reported gains over robot-only training are large, and the human data is collected roughly an order of magnitude faster than teleoperation.
innovation: Aligning human and robot data into a single shared action space so plain co-training works, with no explicit retargeting pipeline.
Visual masking of the human arm to remove the morphology gap the policy would otherwise have to model.
matters: The simplest recipe that works for mixing human and robot data, and it scales with cheap wearable capture rather than robot hours.
limits: Requires the robot action space to be expressible as end-effector poses; in practice parallel-jaw grippers only.
lineage: MimicPlay's human/robot split collapsed into one co-trained policy over Aria-captured data.
